We need to generate a test class covering the test cases listed. Use JUnit5 and Mockito. The focal method is preloadJsonSchema() which calls preloadJsonSchemas(this.schemas.values()). We need to spy on the validator to verify that preloadJsonSchemas is called with appropriate collection. Since preloadJsonSchemas is defined in BaseJsonValidator (probably protected). We can spy the validator and stub the method to capture argument.

We also need to manipulate private field schemas via reflection for some cases (empty map, null map, etc). The test class framework given earlier already has a test for normal case. But we need to incorporate all groups.

We'll create a test class named PropertiesValidatorPreloadJsonSchemaTest (or as given). We'll use @ExtendWith(MockitoExtension.class). We'll have a @Mock ValidationContext. We'll have helper methods to create validator with minimal schema node (maybe empty object) because constructor may populate schemas map based on "properties" in schema node. But for tests where we manually set schemas map, we can use reflection to set the private field.

We need to spy on validator to intercept preloadJsonSchemas call. Since it's defined in BaseJsonValidator, we can use Mockito.spy(validator) and then do doNothing().when(spy).preloadJsonSchemas(anyCollection()); but we need to capture argument. Use ArgumentCaptor<Collection<JsonSchema>>.

Test groups:

1. Empty schemas map: set private map to empty LinkedHashMap, invoke preloadJsonSchema, verify preloadJsonSchemas called with empty collection, no exception.

2. Single schema entry: put one mock schema into map, call, verify called with collection size 1 containing that mock.

3. Multiple schema entries: three mocks, insertion order preserved. Verify order of collection equals list.

4. Null schema value in map: map with key->null, expect NullPointerException from preloadJsonSchemas (since it will iterate and call preloadJsonSchema on null). We can let the real method run; but we need to stub preloadJsonSchemas to just iterate? Actually we are spying and we want to let real method call? If we spy and not stub, the real preloadJsonSchemas will be executed (which likely iterates and calls preloadJsonSchema on each schema). That will cause NPE. So we can let it run and assert exception.

5. Exception propagation from a schema during preload: mock schema whose preloadJsonSchema throws RuntimeException. Insert into map, spy without stubbing preloadJsonSchemas (so it will call real). Expect RuntimeException.

6. Repeated invocation does not alter internal state: map with two mocks, call preloadJsonSchema twice, verify each time same collection (maybe capture each call). Ensure map size unchanged.

7. Order preservation with mixed insertion patterns: map insertion order after removal and re-add. Use LinkedHashMap semantics. Insert A,B,C, remove B, put D with same key as B, final order A,C,D. Verify order.

8. Circular reference schema handling: This is more complex; we can mock two schemas where each's preloadJsonSchema calls something that leads to exception? But we can simulate by making one schema's preloadJsonSchema throw ValidationException (custom). The description expects underlying preload logic to detect circular reference. For test we can just make one schema's preloadJsonSchema throw ValidationException and assert propagation.

9. Null collection handling after map mutation: Use spy to capture collection argument before mutation. After calling preloadJsonSchema, clear map, verify captured collection still contains original schema.

10. Concurrent modification during preload: Mock schema's preloadJsonSchema method that adds a new entry to validator's schemas map. This will cause ConcurrentModificationException when iterating over map values. We need to ensure that the real preloadJsonSchemas iterates over collection (maybe a snapshot?). If it iterates over the collection passed (values()) which is a view, then modification will cause CME. So we can set up map with one mock that on preload adds another entry. Expect CME.

11. Error propagation from schema: mock schema's preloadJsonSchema throws AssertionError. Expect propagate.

12. Null internal schemas map: set private field to null via reflection, invoke preloadJsonSchema, expect NullPointerException.

Implementation details:

- Need method to get and set private field via reflection.

- Use ArgumentCaptor<Collection<JsonSchema>>.

- For verifying order, capture collection and compare to list.

- For repeated invocation, we can use verify(spy, times(2)).preloadJsonSchemas(captor.capture()); then get all captured values.

- For concurrency test, need to catch CME.

Potential imports: java.util.*, org.mockito.*, org.junit.jupiter.api.*, com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.*, com.networknt.schema.*.

We'll write separate @Test methods for each group.

We must not modify @Before/@After methods, but we can add additional setup inside tests.

The earlier test class already includes some code; we can incorporate that as part of the suite, but we need to produce final test class covering all groups. Probably combine everything into one class with multiple test methods.

We'll keep the existing @BeforeEach stub for validationContext.newSchema to return mocks, but many tests will directly set schemas map manually, not using constructor.

We'll need to construct validator with dummy schema node to avoid null pointer in constructor; we can pass an empty object node.

Simplify: create validator using reflection to instantiate with default constructor? There's no default constructor; we need to call the existing constructor (not shown). But we can use new PropertiesValidator("id", MAPPER.createObjectNode(), null, validationContext). That will likely parse properties but not needed.

We'll then replace its schemas map via reflection.
